items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Narrator
Your Black Friday deal could be cheaper in January. One TV was cheaper on a hundred and thirty-four days after the sale. So is the deal real?
Narrator
Consumer group Which tracked a hundred and seventy-five products at eight big retailers for a whole year.
Narrator
eighty-three percent were the same price or cheaper at some other time.
Chars
[smug, deep, rich gold bar, very pleased with himself] Shocking. Truly. I'm shocked.
Narrator
So how does an ordinary price look like a deal?
Narrator
The "was" price. Discounts are often measured from a price the item rarely sold at.
Narrator
Add a countdown clock, and you stop checking.
Narrator
And the trick doesn't stop on Friday.
Narrator
Prices often drop again after the sale. That TV later sold for twenty-seven percent less.
Narrator
That's the mirage: the discount is measured from a price nobody paid.
Narrator
The real test is the price history, not the percent off.
Chars
[nervous, squeaky banknote, trembling] So the sale price was just the price?
Narrator
Comment: what did you buy last Black Friday?
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
